top_categories.workout_context: At mile 60 of 116, glycogen is gone. This workout teaches your body to produce watts on fumes.
Every hard session works better with a bigger aerobic base. At 116 miles, base fitness is the difference between racing and surviving.
Epic Gran Canaria's mountainous paved road rewards steady threshold power. Surging and recovering costs more watts than just holding.
Race-pace efforts that mimic Epic Gran Canaria's demands. Pacing, fueling, and tactical decisions under fatigue. Practice the race before February.
Epic Gran Canaria's mountainous paved road forces constant power changes. Accelerate over rises and out of corners, settle on the open road, and repeat for 116 miles.
When someone attacks on mountainous paved road, you have 10 seconds to respond or you're off the back. This builds that response.
At Epic Gran Canaria, surges push you above threshold and you have to recover while still riding. Over-unders train exactly that.
88–92% FTP is where you'll spend the hardest sustained miles of Epic Gran Canaria. Train it until it feels boring.
116 miles rewards fat oxidation. This volume work shifts your fuel mix so you're still burning fat at hour 5, not bonking at hour 3.
Long rides with hard efforts mixed in. Simulates what Epic Gran Canaria's mountainous paved road actually does to you.
Varied gradients on mountainous paved road demand climbing versatility. Sit the shallow stuff, stand the steep stuff, switch without thinking.
How long can you hold 105% FTP before you blow? At Epic Gran Canaria, that number decides whether you bridge or get dropped.

race_overlay.heat: February in Maspalomas, Gran Canaria, Spain. If the race forecast is hot, build heat exposure gradually before Epic Gran Canaria and rehearse an individualized drinking and electrolyte plan in training. Use your observed sweat response, product tolerance, and professional guidance where relevant instead of a fixed fluid or sodium prescription.
race_overlay.nutrition: Target 60–80g carbs/hour for Epic Gran Canaria’s 116 miles. Start fueling within the first 30 minutes — early fueling prevents late-race collapse. Bonking at mile 60 is a nutrition failure, not a fitness failure.
race_overlay.altitude: Moderate altitude at Epic Gran Canaria. Arrive 2–3 days early. Reduce intensity expectations by 5–10%. Hydrate aggressively.
race_overlay.terrain: Mixed terrain at Epic Gran Canaria requires surface adaptability. Include weekly rides on mountainous paved road to build confidence.

pack_summary: This 10-workout pack focuses on Durability, Endurance, and TT Threshold to prepare you for 116 miles of mountainous paved road in Maspalomas, Gran Canaria, Spain.
